name: Plate-loaded chest press

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat so the handles sit level with the middle of your chest.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Keep your back and head flat on the pad. If the seat lifts you off it, lower the seat one notch.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handles a little wider than shoulder width, with wrists straight.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Load the plates evenly on both sides, then press until the arms are nearly straight without locking out hard.

tips: Keep the shoulder blades back and down; do not let the shoulders roll forward at the bottom.
Lower to a controlled stretch rather than letting the plates drop.

name: Plate-loaded incline press

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat so the handles line up with your upper chest, just below the collarbone.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Sit with your back flat on the pad and both feet flat on the floor or the foot plate.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Use a grip a little wider than shoulder width, with the wrists stacked over the elbows.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Press up and slightly in, stop short of a full lockout, and lower until you feel a stretch across the upper chest.

tips: Keep the lower back on the pad; arching to push more load moves the work away from the upper chest.
Use a weight you can control on the way down, because the incline puts more strain on the shoulders.

name: Plate-loaded iso-lateral row

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat so the handles sit at about mid-chest height when you sit tall.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Brace your chest against the pad and keep your hips in contact with the seat.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold each handle with a neutral or overhand grip, one arm at a time if the arms move independently.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Start with the arms reaching forward, then pull the handles back toward your ribs and squeeze the shoulder blades together.

tips: Keep the chest on the pad and avoid rocking the torso to move the load.
Return slowly until the shoulder blades spread apart at the front.

name: Plate-loaded high row

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat so the handles start a little above shoulder height when your arms are extended.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Lean your chest into the pad and keep your feet flat on the foot plate.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Take a grip wider than the shoulders, palms facing down or in.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Pull the handles down and back toward your upper chest, then let the arms rise until you feel a full stretch in the lats.

tips: Do not lean back to turn the row into a lunge; keep the torso steady.
Lead with the elbows rather than the hands so the pull comes from the back.

name: Plate-loaded shoulder press

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat so the handles start about level with your ears or a little below.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Sit with your back flat against the pad and your spine upright.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handles about shoulder width apart, with the wrists straight.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Press overhead without arching the back, and stop just short of a full lockout.

tips: Keep the ribs down; leaning back turns the press into a lower back exercise.
Lower the handles until they are about level with your ears before you press again.

name: Leg press

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Adjust the seat back so your lower back and hips stay on the pad at the bottom of the movement.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Place the feet about shoulder width apart on the platform, toes turned slightly out.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the side handles firmly to keep your hips pressed back.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Release the safety catch, then lower the sled until the knees reach about 90 degrees or the hips begin to lift.

tips: Do not lock the knees at the top; stop just short of full extension.
If the lower back starts to round off the pad, the range is too deep for that load.

name: Hack squat
brandNote: Plate-loaded, angled sled with shoulder pads

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Set the shoulder pads on top of the shoulders, under the trapezius, not against the neck.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Place the feet on the platform about hip width apart, with the toes turned out slightly.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handles at your sides to steady the body.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Unlock the sled, lower under control until the thighs are near parallel or a little deeper, then drive up without locking out hard.

tips: Keep the heels down and the knees tracking over the toes.
Stop the descent before the lower back starts to round off the pad.

name: Hip thrust machine

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Set the hip pad so it sits across the hip crease when your upper back rests on the bench.

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Sit with the upper back against the bench and the hip pad across the hips.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Place both feet flat about hip width apart, with the shins vertical at the top of the rep.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Drive the hips up until the torso is level with the floor, squeeze the glutes, then lower under control.

tips: Keep the chin tucked and the ribs down; do not hyperextend the lower back at the top.
Pause briefly at the top, since the hip extension is where the glutes do most of the work.

name: Seated chest press machine

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat so the handles line up with the middle of your chest.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Keep your back flat against the backrest with the shoulder blades touching it.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Use handles about shoulder width apart, with the wrists in line with the forearms.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin under a weight you can control through the full range, then press without shrugging the shoulders.

tips: Keep the shoulders down rather than rising toward the ears.
Lower at a steady pace so the chest, not momentum, does the work.

name: Pec deck

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat so the arm pads sit level with the middle of your chest when your elbows are bent at about 90 degrees.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Sit with the back and head against the backrest and the forearms resting on the pads.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin under a weight you can move smoothly through the full range.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Bring the pads together in front of the chest in a wide arc, then let them open slowly until you feel a stretch.

tips: Keep the elbows soft and the arc wide; do not let the pads slam together.
Lean forward only slightly, since leaning far forward moves the work onto the shoulders.

name: Lat pulldown

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the thigh pad so it holds the thighs down firmly, with the knees under the pad.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Sit tall and keep the thigh pad snug on the thighs for the whole set.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Take a wide overhand grip, a little wider than the shoulders.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin under your chosen weight, then reach up to the bar with the arms fully extended.

tips: Pull the bar to the upper chest by driving the elbows down, not by leaning far back.
Let the arms straighten fully at the top to get the full stretch through the lats.

name: Seated row machine

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Rest the chest firmly on the pad with the arms reaching forward and the handles at about shoulder height.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Keep the feet flat on the floor or the foot plate, knees slightly bent.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handles with a neutral or overhand grip, arms straight.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin under your weight, then pull the handles back to the ribs and squeeze the shoulder blades together.

tips: Keep the chest on the pad; rocking the torso to start the pull takes the work away from the back.
Return slowly until the shoulder blades spread apart at the front.

name: Shoulder press machine

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat so the handles start about level with your ears.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Sit with the back flat against the backrest.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handles about shoulder width apart, with the wrists straight.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin, then press up without arching the lower back, stopping just short of a full lockout.

tips: Keep the ribs down; arching the back turns the press into a lower back exercise.
Lower the handles to about ear height rather than further, to keep the shoulders comfortable.

name: Lateral raise machine

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat so the pivot of the arm pads lines up with your shoulder joint.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Place the forearms or the elbow pads against the pads, just below the wrist.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Choose a light weight with the pin, then start with the arms resting at the sides.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Raise the pads out to the side until the upper arms are level with the floor, then lower with control.

tips: Lead with the elbows and keep a slight bend, so the side of the shoulder does the work.
Do not shrug the shoulders up as you lift; keep the traps quiet.

name: Leg extension

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat back so the pivot of the lever lines up with the front of the knee joint.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Adjust the pad so it rests on the lower shins, just above the ankles.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the side handles to stay seated and steady.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin, then extend the legs until the knees are straight without snapping into the lock.

tips: Lower slowly, since the lowering part of the rep carries much of the work.
Keep the speed steady on the way up rather than swinging the weight.

name: Seated leg curl

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat so the pivot lines up with the back of the knee, and the thigh pad sits flat on the thighs.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Adjust the back pad so the lever rests on the back of the lower legs, just above the ankles.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin under a weight you can move smoothly, then start with the legs straight.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handles to stay in the seat.

tips: Keep the hips pressed into the seat; lifting them off it turns the set into a cheat.
Stop the curl short of the point where the hips begin to rise.

name: Lying leg curl

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Lie face down with the hips pressed into the bench and the knee joint at the edge of the bench.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Set the pad so it rests on the back of the lower legs, just above the heels.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handles above the bench to steady the upper body.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin under a weight you can control, then start with the legs straight.

tips: Keep the hips flat on the bench; lifting them shortens the work.
Lower with control until the legs are straight, rather than letting the stack drop.

name: Hip abductor machine

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat height so the pads sit against the outside of the thighs, just above the knees.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Sit upright with the back against the backrest and the pads snug on the outer thighs.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin under a light weight to start, then build up gradually.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Open the legs slowly against the pads, pause, and return until the thighs are close but not crashing together.

tips: Lean forward slightly for more glute work and sit upright for more outer thigh work.
Avoid rocking the torso to move the load.

name: Hip adductor machine

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat height so the pads sit on the inside of the thighs, just above the knees.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Sit upright with the back against the backrest and the pads snug on the inner thighs.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin under a light weight and build up gradually.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Bring the legs together slowly against the pads, pause, then let them open until you feel a stretch without pain.

tips: Keep the back against the backrest; leaning forward to push the pads moves the work away from the inner thighs.
Control the opening part of the rep, since the stretch is part of the set.

name: Standing calf raise

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Place the shoulder pads on top of the shoulders, under the trapezius, and hold the handles.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Stand with the balls of the feet on the edge of the plate, heels free to drop.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin under a weight you can control, then release the stop.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Rise onto the toes as high as you can, pause, then lower until the calves are fully stretched.

tips: Use a full stretch at the bottom; short partial reps leave much of the calf unworked.
Keep the knees straight but not locked, and do not bounce at the bottom.

name: Seated calf raise

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the thigh pad so it rests firmly on the thighs, just above the knees.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Place the balls of the feet on the plate with the heels free to drop.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin under a weight you can control.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Raise the heels as high as possible, pause, then lower them fully into the stretch.

tips: Keep the knees bent throughout, which shifts the work to the deeper calf muscle under the calf.
Avoid bouncing at the bottom of the rep.

name: Preacher curl machine

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat so the edge of the pad sits at the armpits.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Rest the upper arms flat on the pad with the elbows just beyond its edge.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handle about shoulder width apart, palms up.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin under a light weight and start with the arms almost straight.

tips: Keep the upper arms on the pad; lifting the elbows to finish the curl is a cheat.
Lower until the arms are almost straight, since the bottom of the rep stretches the biceps.

name: Triceps extension machine

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat so the pivot lines up with the outer edge of the elbow joint.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Place the back of the forearms against the pad, with the upper arms pressed to the sides.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handle with a neutral grip.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin under a weight you can control, then start with the elbows bent at about 90 degrees.

tips: Keep the upper arms still; if the elbows drift forward the shoulders take over.
Extend until the arms are straight without locking out hard.

name: Assisted pull-up and dip machine

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Step onto the knee pad, which carries part of your body weight; the more assistance you choose, the more it carries.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handles with a grip you can keep for the whole set.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Set the assistance so the rep is challenging but controlled, since each setting changes how much help you get.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Start from arms straight for a dip or from a full hang for a pull-up, then move under control.

tips: Do not drop onto the pad between reps; keep the movement controlled.
Keep the body still rather than swinging to start each rep.

name: Ab crunch machine

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat height so the pivot sits about level with the hips.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Rest the chest lightly against the pad with the back straight.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handles lightly; the hands guide the movement but do not pull it.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin under a light weight and begin with the torso upright.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Crunch the upper torso toward the thighs by curling the spine, then return slowly.

tips: Curl the ribs toward the hips rather than pulling with the arms.
Breathe out as you crunch and let the torso return with control.

name: Cable crossover

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Set both pulleys with the pins at about shoulder height for a mid-chest fly, or lower for an upper chest angle.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Take a handle in each hand, with a slight bend in the elbows.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Step forward to create tension, with one foot ahead for balance and the chest open.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Bring the hands together in front of the chest in a wide arc, then open them back slowly.

tips: Keep the elbows soft and the arc wide; do not turn the fly into a press.
Keep the torso still, since leaning in to move the stack wastes the set.

name: Adjustable cable station

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Insert the pin under the weight you want, then check that the stack moves freely.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Set the pulley height for the exercise: high for pushdowns and face pulls, low for curls and kickbacks.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Choose the attachment (straight bar, rope or single handle) and hold it with a secure grip.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Set your stance with the feet apart for balance, with the working side just in front of the stack.

tips: Keep the stance steady and the core braced; do not lean into the weight for momentum.
Check the pulley height before each exercise, since a wrong height changes the line of pull.

name: Smith machine
brandNote: Barbell on vertical guide rails, safety hooks

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Set the safety hooks just below the lowest point you will reach, so the bar can be caught.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Set the bar at a height where you can unrack it with your legs, then turn it onto the hooks.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Place the feet slightly in front of the bar path, with the bar over the middle of the foot.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Unrack with a controlled step back, then keep the bar on a fixed path for the whole set.

tips: Set the hooks before every set; a set without them is unsafe.
The bar path is fixed, so keep the feet in position and do not let the hips drift.

name: Dumbbell rack

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Choose a pair with both dumbbells the same weight, and check the handles are clean and secure.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Lift each dumbbell from the rack with a firm grip and a straight wrist.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Stand with the feet apart for balance before lifting, and keep the weight close to the body.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Return the dumbbells to the same rack spot after each set rather than leaving them on the floor.

tips: Grip the handle, not the plates; a loose grip makes the wrists work harder.
Keep the area around the rack clear to avoid trips and dropped weights.

name: Flat bench

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Check the bench sits flat and is stable on the floor before you lie down.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Lie with the head, upper back and hips on the pad, feet flat on the floor.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: For a barbell press, set the bar on the rack hooks at about the height of your chest.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Lift the bar off the rack with straight arms over the chest and keep the hips in place.

tips: Use spotter pins or the rack safeties for heavy sets.
Keep the feet flat and drive through the floor; do not lift the hips off the pad.

name: Incline bench

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the bench to a shallow incline, usually about 30 to 45 degrees, and check it is locked in place.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Lie with the upper back and head on the pad, feet flat on the floor.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Set the bar on the hooks at about the height of your upper chest.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Unrack the bar with straight arms and keep the shoulder blades pinned back on the pad.

tips: A steep incline moves the work onto the front shoulders, so keep the angle shallow.
Lower the bar to the upper chest, not to the neck.

name: Adjustable bench

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the backrest to the angle the exercise calls for.

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Lock the backrest at that angle with its pin before you load it.

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Sit or lie with the back supported by the pad and the feet flat on the floor.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Rest the dumbbells on your thighs, then lift them into position with the hands.

tips: Check the lock before each set; a backrest that moves under load can drop the weight.
Lift the dumbbells with the hands on the thighs, then move them into position with control.

name: Squat rack

setup.label: Pin
setup.text: Set the safety bars just below the lowest point of your squat or bench, so the bar can rest on them.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Set the hooks at about shoulder height for squats, and at chest or shoulder height for presses.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Stand under the bar with it resting on the upper back for squats, then unrack with a controlled step.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Step back with a few small steps, feet about shoulder width apart and toes slightly out.

tips: Set the safety bars every time, so a missed rep lands on them rather than on you.
Check the hooks are level before loading, since an uneven rack shifts the bar.

name: Olympic barbell

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Choose the grip width the exercise calls for, and note where your hands sit on the knurling so you can repeat it.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Load the plates evenly on both sides and fasten the collars firmly.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Keep the bar close to the body from the start position, and move it in a straight line.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Stand with the feet under the bar, about hip width apart, with the bar over the middle of the foot.

tips: Check the collars are tight before every set; a loose collar slides and shifts the load.
Keep the bar close to the body, since a bar that drifts forward adds strain to the lower back.

name: EZ curl bar

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Pick the angled grip that feels comfortable on the wrists; the bends let the wrists sit more naturally.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Load the plates evenly and fasten the collars. The bar weighs 10 kg empty.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Check the collars are secure before lifting so nothing slides during the set.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Stand with the feet about hip width apart and the bar held in front of the thighs.

tips: Keep the elbows pinned to the sides; swinging the torso turns the curl into a cheat.
Use the angled grips rather than the straight section if the wrists feel strained.

name: Trap bar
brandNote: Hexagonal frame, handles at the sides

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Stand in the centre of the frame with the midfoot under its middle, and grip the handles at your sides.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handles with a neutral grip, arms straight and hanging.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Set the feet about hip width apart, with the shins close to the frame.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Brace, push the floor away and stand up tall, then lower the bar under control.

tips: The frame lets you start more upright, but the back still needs bracing before every pull.
Lower under control rather than dropping the weight, which jolts the back.

name: Pull-up bar

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Choose an overhand, underhand or neutral grip, a little wider than the shoulders for pull-ups.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Hang with the arms straight and the shoulders packed down rather than hanging from the joints.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: If you need a step, use a stable box below the bar and step off once your grip is set.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Pull up until the chin clears the bar, then lower to a full hang.

tips: Start each rep from a full hang; kipping shortens the range.
Draw the elbows down toward the ribs rather than pulling with the arms alone.

name: Dip station

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Grip the bars with straight arms and the elbows close to the sides.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Keep the legs bent behind you, or straight in front if you need the feet free.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Keep the feet together, or crossed behind you, to stay balanced.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Lower until the upper arms are a little below parallel to the floor, then press back up.

tips: Lean slightly forward to bias the chest, and stay upright to bias the triceps.
Stop the descent before the shoulders roll forward into the bottom position.

name: Back extension bench

setup.label: Pad
setup.text: Set the pad so it sits just above the hip crease, with the body folded at the hips.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Hook the feet under the anchor pads and keep the heels steady.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Start with the torso lowered and the hips on the pad, so the body forms a straight line from head to knees at the top.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Cross the arms over the chest, or hold a light weight there.

tips: Lift only to a straight line from head to knees; going higher bends the lower back.
Move slowly and avoid snapping the back at the top.

name: Treadmill

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Stand on the side rails with the safety clip attached to your clothing before starting the belt.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Set the speed low and let the belt reach pace before stepping onto it.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handrails lightly for balance, not for support.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Slow the belt to a stop before stepping off onto the side rails.

tips: Keep a steady stride and an upright posture; do not lean on the rails.
Set the speed and incline before you start running, because changing them mid-stride is risky.

name: Incline treadmill

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Set the incline with the controls before you start, and make adjustments while standing on the side rails.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Step onto the side rails, attach the safety clip, then start the belt at a walking pace.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Keep the steps short and the posture upright, since the incline loads the calves and glutes more.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Slow the belt to a stop before stepping off.

tips: Keep each step short; reaching far with the feet strains the calves and hamstrings.
Hold the handrails lightly; holding on hard reduces the work and tilts the hips.

name: Stair climber

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Place each foot fully on a step, with the weight centred over it.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Set the level and speed on the display before you start, beginning at the lowest setting.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Rest the hands lightly on the rails; the rails are for balance, not support.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Step at a steady pace and stop the steps before stepping off.

tips: Stand tall and do not lean on the rails, since leaning takes work away from the legs.
Keep the knees in line with the feet and avoid snapping the knees at the bottom of each step.

name: Upright bike

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Set the seat height so the knee has a slight bend at the bottom of each pedal stroke.

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Place the balls of the feet on the pedals and fasten the straps if the bike has them.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handlebars lightly with the back upright.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Choose the resistance and start pedalling at an easy pace before raising the load.

tips: Set the seat height properly; too low strains the knees, and too high rocks the hips.
Keep the shoulders relaxed rather than hunched over the bars.

name: Rowing machine

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Strap the feet in with the heel cups close to the heels, so the ankles sit under the straps.

setup.label: Seat
setup.text: Sit on the seat with the knees bent and the shins close to vertical at the catch.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handle with an overhand grip, arms straight, and the body leaning slightly forward.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Push with the legs first, then lean back and draw the handle to the lower ribs; reverse the sequence on the return.

tips: Drive with the legs first; pulling with the arms early tires the back quickly.
Keep the lower back neutral, since rounding forward under load strains it.

name: Elliptical

setup.label: Foot plate
setup.text: Stand on the pedals with the feet flat and centred, not on the toes.

setup.label: Grip
setup.text: Hold the handles lightly with the arms relaxed.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Set the resistance and the ramp level, then start the stride slowly before increasing the pace.

setup.label: Other
setup.text: Keep the back upright and the stride smooth, and step off only after the pedals have stopped.

tips: Keep the stride smooth and the back upright; leaning on the handles reduces the work.
Keep the knees soft at the bottom of each stride.
